history: The residual of 008, and the reason 008's fix needed a second pass. Moving MAX_MEM into parse_program closed almost everything, but the guard compared the declared LENGTH against MAX_MEM while codegen counted the cells the program actually needs -- so lengths of exactly 1048575 and 1048576 parsed and then failed in codegen, a two-wide band where interpret_source would still allocate a million cells for a program the compiler would not build. A guard that measures the wrong quantity closes every case except the ones where the difference between the two quantities is what matters. Now both count the same thing.
note: Exactly MAX_MEM. A program declaring an array of 1048576 cells also needs a cell for its input and one for its output window, so the total is over the limit and both lowerings refuse it -- at parse, before either runs. 1048574 still compiles, which is the point of pinning this from both sides: the boundary is the TOTAL cell count, not the declared length.
signature: oracle-accepts compiler-refuses: CodegenError: program needs N cells, over the N limit
source: input a; arr m[1048576]; output a;
